S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is defined by marked fear or anxiety focused on a specific object or situation, with an immediate fear response and active avoidance or endurance with intense distress, out of proportion to the actual danger. It is typically persistent and impairing, and is distinguished from panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, or agoraphobia by the fear being tied to a circumscribed cue rather than unexpected attacks, social evaluation, or broad difficulty escaping.

patient.stressor: Thirteen months ago, Norman was overseeing a fast-moving light-commercial build when a temporary stair tower shifted under him, leaving him with broken ribs and several weeks away from the site. When he returned, elevated platforms, roof edges, and scaffold inspections began to carry a fear that was far beyond the objective safety measures he had always trusted, and the fear appeared as soon as he had to approach those areas. Over the following year and one month, he increasingly delegated height-related inspections, altered schedules to avoid walking upper levels, and lost credibility with crews and subcontractors because key decisions were delayed. He entered psychiatric care after an occupational health evaluation, requested by his employer’s insurer following repeated missed safety walk-throughs, recommended treatment for a specific phobia rather than further physical restriction.

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: I’m here because every time I have to get near a scaffold, roof edge, or upper platform now, my head tells me I’m about to go over even when I can see the rails are in place and I know the setup is supposed to be safe.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: The second I step onto temporary stairs or even walk toward an open upper floor, my chest tightens, my hands get wet, and I feel like my legs might lock up before I can make myself take another step.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I’ve been handing off height inspections to my foremen, moving meetings to the ground level, and when I absolutely have to go up, I keep someone right beside me and rush through it scared the whole time.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve missed or delayed enough upper-level walk-throughs that my crews and subcontractors have started questioning my calls, and my employer’s insurer pushed for an occupational health review because I wasn’t completing key safety inspections.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on since the stair tower accident about thirteen months ago.
